newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money falls back to 30 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money falls back to 30 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money fell back to 30 percent on Friday from a record 125 percent in the morning after some offers emerged, dealers said.
They said rupiah offers by some state banks relieved the tightness, knocking overnight rates down immediately, but driving spot rupiah lower against the dollar.
Swap rates were also easing, with overnight swap edging lower to around 10.0 points, equivalent to some 49 percent, after rising to a high of 26.5 points, or 360 percent.
One-month money eased to 25/30 percent from 45 percent.
The central bank maintained its bilateral rates for central bank certificates (SBIs) on Friday.

The bank kept its overnight (three-day) SBIs at 15.0 percent, four-to-six day SBIs at 16.0 percent, one-week at 10.5, two-week at 11.0, one-month at 11.625, three at 11.5, six at 12.125 and one-year at 12.75 percent.
Dealers said the extreme tightness resulted from central bank dollar selling on Wednesday, which was to mature on Friday.

Central Bank Governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said the bank sold some $500 million in the spot market to support the rupiah on Wednesday, resulting in a drain of more than one trillion rupiah from the market.
"It shouldn't be a surprise. But the market still got squeezed," one dealer said.
A balance of 650 billion rupiah was available to the market from maturing central bank papers on Friday.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 47.22 percent, compared with 23.69 percent on Wednesday.
